candidates.title: vg.lua honest player's machine cache does not keep the spacing the manual promises: retained input boundaries end up 1.25x-1.5x (2x at capacity 2) the current minimum gap apart, and at non-power-of-two offsets
candidates.component: Verification-game recipe doc/recipes/vg.lua (honest player's machine cache), described in doc/README.md '### The player'
candidates.role: Support (the vg.lua player is a demonstration operator that no deployment runs; it stands in for the honest operator)
candidates.location: doc/recipes/vg.lua machine_cache_methods:consider (lines 264-296) and find_nearest_entry/nearer_not_past_epoch_input_offset_or (298-334); doc/README.md lines 9806-9823 (algorithm) and 9859-9863 ('The machines are evenly spaced in the epoch, in the sense that the gap between consecutive machines is either the current minimum gap or half of it')
candidates.description: The manual states that the cache keeps the machines evenly spaced: every gap between consecutive retained machines is either the current minimum gap or half of it. The implementation does not keep that invariant. When the cache is full, consider() removes the first entry whose gap to its predecessor is below input_gap and appends the new machine at the end. Removing an entry merges two gaps into one, and the merged gap can exceed input_gap. Appending a new entry after input_gap has doubled can also leave gaps that are neither input_gap nor input_gap/2. With the real vg.lua code at capacity 8: after input 15, input_gap = 2 and the entries are {0,2,4,6,9,11,13,15}, so the gap 6->9 is 3. After input 100, input_gap = 16 and the entries are {0,19,39,47,55,63,79,95}, with gaps 19 and 20. After 65,536 inputs, input_gap = 8192 and the entries are {0,10239,20479,28671,40959,49151,57343,65535}, with gaps 10239, 10240 and 12288. Across capacities 4 to 32 the largest gap reaches 1.5 times the current input_gap, and 2 times at capacity 2. The cache keeps no machine inside such a gap. A machine that the player must move to a position inside it (run_to_position through nearer_not_past_epoch_input_offset_or) therefore replays up to 1.5 times as many inputs as the manual's bound allows, on every bisection or proof that lands there.
candidates.trigger: Anyone who posts inputs: an epoch with more inputs than the cache capacity (default 8) is enough, and the effect grows with the number of inputs. A dishonest player can then steer the bisection into the widest gap, because the honest player must answer every midpoint.
candidates.reachability: Reached on every epoch with more than about 2 x capacity inputs. No guest behavior is needed, since it depends only on the input count. The real code reproduces it with mock machines, so no emulator state is involved.
candidates.rating_steps: 1. Out of scope? No exclusion applies. The trigger is the number of posted inputs, which any input sender controls (section 7: 'Send any number of inputs the deployment accepts'). It is not an application's outputs or yields, and it does not need the machine API. 2. Role: the vg.lua player is Support (AUDIT.md lists 'The PRT player and bridge in doc/recipes ... Support. No production deployment runs the player'. The verification-game player is likewise a demonstration operator). It stands in for the honest operator. Section 3: 'A defect that only a support component shows is Medium when it would rate High or Critical in the role the component stands in for ... the honest operator for an implementation of an operator ... Any other support defect is Low.' 3. High/Medium cases: as an honest-operator defect it would be a constant-factor (at most 1.5x, or 2x at capacity 2) increase in the cost of reaching a disputed position, which R12 bounds ('Reaching that position costs at most the mcycles from the nearest retained input boundary'). The High case covers 'A defect that lets the guest, or host load that the deployment was sized for, multiply the worst-case cost of an operation listed in R12 by a constant factor'. Here input senders trigger it, not the guest or host load, and the spacing the manual promises already allows gaps of up to about 2n/capacity. The worst case in absolute terms is therefore almost unchanged: max gap / (n/capacity) stays at or below about 2.0 in simulation, both with and without the defect. The contradiction is literal, but its cost effect is within the factor the promised design already allows. 'A contradiction between the manual and the behavior on a security-relevant point ... takes the severity it would have if the manual were right.' Whether cache spacing is security-relevant decides the rating. If it is (it bounds the honest player's per-match cost, R12), the stand-in rating is at most High as a constant factor, so Medium for support. If it is not, Low. 4. Critical: no. The cost stays linear, and the factor is constant and small. 5. Low otherwise. Preferred: Low (a manual claim about a demonstration cache that is wrong by a constant factor below the worst case the promised spacing already permits). Alternative: Medium (support stand-in for a High R12 constant factor, if the spacing claim counts as a security-relevant promise). Related to, but distinct from, R3-VARGROWTH-1, which is about the cache capacity itself (8 boundaries per epoch), not the spacing invariant.
candidates.claimed_severity: Low (alternative: Medium as a support stand-in for a High R12 constant-factor case)
candidates.threat_to_goal: It does not break the goal. It weakens the honest (demonstration) player's per-match cost bound that the manual states. A production operator that copies the documented cache design ('In production, the cache implementation could instead use stored machines, without changing the outside-facing interface') would inherit up to 1.5x more replay per match than the manual leads it to provision for, which eats into A7's clock margin.
candidates.evidence: Ran /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-machine-emulator/549e7dd9-06ba-5ccf-8b17-f8cce9526655/scratchpad/campaign/r7/MANGAME/cache-real.lua, which loads the real vg.lua through require('vg') with bugs/env.sh and drives vg.new_machine_cache/consider with mock machines. At capacity 8 the first violation comes after input 15: input_gap=2, entries={0,2,4,6,9,11,13,15}. At n=100: input_gap=16, entries={0,19,39,47,55,63,79,95}. At n=65536: input_gap=8192, entries={0,10239,20479,28671,40959,49151,57343,65535}, with 147,398 violating (step, entry) pairs. A port of the algorithm (cache-sim3.lua) shows the worst entry gap / input_gap is 1.5 for capacities 4-32 and 2.0 for capacity 2.
candidates.test_idea: Create vg.new_machine_cache with a mock machine (fork_server, set_cleanup_call, shutdown_server, get_root_hash), call consider(i, mock) for i = 1..100 with capacity 8, and after each call assert that every gap between consecutive entries equals cache.input_gap or cache.input_gap // 2, as the manual states. It fails deterministically after input 15, with gap 3 while input_gap is 2. The test passes once the cache keeps the invariant, or once the manual states the real bound.
